summary: 10 comment-endorsed discoveries: coding tools, desktop workflows, games, and an emergency-care course.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: C++ Insights
items.source_story_title: C++ Insights – See your source code with the eyes of a Compiler
items.summary: C++ code explorer that reveals how lambdas and range-based loops work.
items.why_included: A commenter demonstrates its teaching value with a concrete lambda example.
items.evidence: sltkr praises the tool for explaining C++ lambdas and provides an example that also exposes range-based loop mechanics.

evidence_sources.author: sltkr
evidence_sources.excerpt: But it's a great example of how this tool is useful to learn about those things (of course you could also read the C++ standard but who has time for that?)

items.name: AeroSpace
items.summary: Configurable macOS tiling window manager that leaves System Integrity Protection enabled.
items.why_included: Two weeks of positive first-hand use provide a concrete desktop-workflow endorsement.
items.evidence: rubslopes reports a great experience after two weeks, highlighting configurability and not needing to disable SIP.

evidence_sources.author: rubslopes
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using Aerospace on MacOS for 2 weeks and having a great experience with it. Very configurable, and it doesn't require you to deactivate SIP like yabai.

items.name: T3 Code
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Pi pod – Run your pi coding agent in sandboxes on your own server
items.summary: Open-source coding-agent control interface; one user runs it successfully in Kubernetes.
items.why_included: A specific self-hosted setup is positively endorsed rather than merely listed.
items.evidence: fratellobigio says T3 Code works well with a Claude subscription in Kubernetes, using persistent storage for configs and repos; the comment notes no official Docker image.

evidence_sources.author: fratellobigio
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use a T3 Code pod in a kubernetes Deployment (sadly no official Docker image), with a PVC so configs and cloned repos survive pod restarts. Seems to work quite well with my Claude subscription (no GPU in my homelab yet)

items.name: Orca
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Offrun – manage every coding agent from one workspace
items.summary: Coding-agent development environment with parallel worktrees, terminals, diffs, and mobile access.
items.why_included: A long-time user explicitly calls the experience great while explaining an unmet workflow need.
items.evidence: phildenhoff praises long-term Orca use, but describes frustration with finding blocking questions buried in agent conversations.

evidence_sources.author: phildenhoff
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used Orca for ages and that was great; I'm just tired of having to scroll back through a convo to find that "one last blocking question" that Claude or Codex spit out 15 tool calls and subagent messages ago.

items.name: OpenCrow (pkulak fork)
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Pi pod – Run your pi coding agent in sandboxes on your own server
items.summary: Matrix AI-assistant project; its maintainer praises selective desktop access through Nix containers.
items.why_included: The linked personal setup has a concrete, positively described access-control benefit.
items.evidence: pkulak endorses using systemd containers in Nix to selectively expose desktop resources and links their OpenCrow fork; this is maintainer context, not an independent security audit.

evidence_sources.author: pkulak
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Systemd containers in Nix. That’s really cool because I can selectively link in the parts of my desktop that I want it to have access to.

items.name: Hole Punch
items.source_story_title: Hole Punch: Sling your spaceship around gravitational fields
items.summary: Browser physics puzzle that steers a spaceship using black-hole gravity; mobile controls need care.
items.why_included: Direct gameplay praise comes with specific, useful mobile-control caveats.
items.evidence: rkagerer calls it a great game but finds mobile controls imprecise.

evidence_sources.author: rkagerer
evidence_sources.excerpt: Great game, though the controls on mobile are a bit too imprecise.

items.name: Interplanetary: Enhanced Edition
items.source_story_title: Hole Punch: Sling your spaceship around gravitational fields
items.summary: Turn-based planetary artillery game where shots bend through solar-system gravity fields.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly recommends it as a playable gravity-artillery game.
items.evidence: x______________ tells readers to check out Interplanetary in a discussion of turn-based space artillery.

evidence_sources.author: x______________
evidence_sources.excerpt: Another version of this idea has been out for some time now, check out Interplanetary[0]

items.name: Arctic Eggs
items.source_story_title: Mike Tomlin spent 12 years building a Minecraft city
items.summary: Surreal sci-fi cooking game about frying illegal eggs in Antarctica.
items.why_included: An explicit play recommendation surfaces an off-topic indie-game discovery.
items.evidence: polytely directly urges readers to play Arctic Eggs while discussing celebrities' interest in indie games.

items.name: William and Sly 2
items.source_story_title: Newgrounds.com – A community of games, music, and art
items.summary: Atmospheric fox-exploration platformer remembered fondly by a longtime Newgrounds player.
items.why_included: A first-hand favorite is named clearly and has a direct game page.
items.evidence: carefree-bob names William and Sly and William and Sly 2 among their favorite games from the site.

evidence_sources.author: carefree-bob
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used to play flash games on this site, one of my favorites was "William and Sly" and also "William and Sly 2".
